_meta.description: Seed derivation-link overrides: agent-classified verdicts for all Exclude/OneWayOnly pairs with derived FrequencyRank <= 10000 (600 pairs). Overrides the automatic sense-coverage rule in --build-derivations. See PLAN_DerivationalRedundancy.md §4.2.

洒落 covers the 'joke/pun' sense predictably, but base 洒落る also means 'to dress stylishly', a sense the noun doesn't carry.
数多く is the fully regular く-adverb of 数多い with no added meaning.
聞こえ specifically means 'reputation/how one is perceived' (世間の聞こえ), a lexicalized social sense beyond plain audibility.
取り入る ('to curry favor') and 取り入れる ('to incorporate/adopt/harvest') are unrelated lexical verbs that only coincidentally share the 取り stem; not a real potential relationship.
落とし narrows to 'a missing item / something forgotten', a specific lexicalized sense beyond plain 'dropping'.
散らし is the well-known concrete noun for 'a flyer/leaflet' (チラシ), a lexicalized object-sense unrelated to plain 'scattering'.
巡り carries specific senses 'circumference/girth (of a measured object)' and 'pilgrimage', both lexicalized extensions beyond plain 'going around'.
追って ('later on, shortly') is a fixed formal adverb (追って連絡します); the shift from 'chasing' to a temporal 'afterward' needs idiomatic knowledge.
見張り ('watch, lookout') is the predictable noun form; base 見張る also means 'to open one's eyes wide', a sense the noun doesn't carry.

This entry mislabels the source: 高め ('somewhat high') actually derives from the adjective 高い via the め-suffix (see the correctly-tagged 高い→高め pair), not from the verb 高める; as a masu-stem noun of 高める it isn't predictable.
高め is the fully regular め-suffix ('somewhat high') pattern; base 高い also covers abstract/loudness senses (声が高い) that the purely gradable-degree noun doesn't carry.
反射的に is the fully regular 的+に adverb of 反射的 with no added meaning.
切り抜ける ('to get through/overcome a difficulty') is a lexicalized metaphorical verb (fighting one's way through obstacles), not simply 'can cut out'; not predictable from base+potential.
柔らかさ is the plain, fully transparent -さ nominalization of 柔らかい with no unrelated sense either side.
Same target noun 柔らかさ; the na-adjective 柔らか also has no unrelated sense, so the -さ form is fully predictable and adds nothing extra.
大きめ is the regular め-suffix pattern; base 大きい also covers abstract senses like 'loud', which the purely size-graded noun doesn't carry.
隠し ('hiding, concealing') and its common adjectival-prefix use ('hidden', as in 隠しポケット) are reasonably predictable from 'to hide' plus the noun-form rule.
断り covers both 'declining' and 'advance notice/permission' (先に断っておく), both of which are genuine senses of the base verb 断る itself, so the noun stays within the base's range.
お宝 stays within 'treasure/valuable possession' (including modern casual use for a prized item); no meaning falls outside the honorific relation.
締め has accrued many domain-specific lexicalized uses (closing accounts, the finishing dish/ritual at a meal or event), well beyond plain 'tying/fastening'.
Same target noun 締め/〆; base 〆る itself already carries the specialized senses 'to total up' and 'to kill (fish/poultry)', and the noun's domain-specific uses aren't predictable from a plain gloss.
迎え ('person sent to meet a visitor') is a natural but specific person-referring extension; predictable enough for base→derived but not guaranteed both ways.
占む is essentially a classical/archaic predecessor of the modern verb 占める, not a genuine potential derivation, and is too obscure for a learner to encounter standalone.
並び ('line, row, rank') is the predictable noun form; base 並ぶ also means 'to rival/match', a sense the concrete noun doesn't carry.
ご連絡 is the plain polite prefixation of the verbal noun 連絡 with no meaning shift; ご+action-noun rarely drifts the way お+concrete-noun does.
張り specifically describes physical 'tension/resilience/firmness' (of skin, hair) and figurative 'vanity' (見栄を張る-related), lexicalized senses beyond plain 'to stretch/paste'.
突き立てる adds a forceful/violent connotation ('to stab, thrust violently') not present in the base's more neutral 'to stick up/rise sharply'.
何気なく is the fully regular く-adverb of 何気ない with no added meaning.
高すぎる is the fully productive すぎる ('too much') construction; base 高い also covers senses (e.g. loud) that don't combine the same way in this specific derived form.
住まい ('dwelling, residence') is the standard, fully transparent noun form of 'to reside' with nothing extra either side.
In modern Japanese 滅多 is used almost exclusively inside the fixed adverbial 滅多に...ない; base 滅多 also has an archaic standalone adjectival sense ('reckless') the adverb doesn't teach.
挫ける is the direct intransitive counterpart of 挫く with closely parallel meaning ('to be disheartened' vs 'to discourage'); nothing extra either side.

硬さ covers 'firmness/hardness' predictably; the extra 'honesty' gloss reflects 硬い's figurative 'stiff/formal (personality)' sense that a learner wouldn't derive from the plain physical adjective alone.
甘え ('overdependence, presumed acceptance') is the direct nominalization of the well-known psychological concept; kept one-way as a mild safety margin though the match is close.
回し is the specific sumo term for the wrestler's belt/loincloth (mawashi), a lexicalized object-sense unrelated to plain 'turning'.
聞き覚え ('memory of having heard before') is the direct, transparent nominalization with nothing extra either side.
囁き ('whisper, murmur') is the predictable noun form of 'to whisper'; kept one-way given base's additional 'to rumor/rumour' sense that the noun doesn't clearly carry.
曇り covers 'fog on glass/a mirror' and 'a flaw/cloudiness in a gem', both natural but domain-specific metaphorical extensions of 'clouding over' that need some exposure to recognize.
生き残り ('survivor, relic') is a natural person/thing-denoting extension of 'to survive'; kept one-way as the person-reference isn't guaranteed obvious from the verb alone.
取り調べ ('police investigation, examination') is the direct, fully transparent nominalization of 'to investigate' with nothing extra either side.

引きつれる (written 引き連れる, 'to bring/take someone along') is an entirely different verb from 引きつる (written 引き攣る, 'to have a cramp/twitch'); a false pairing from a homophone-adjacent reading, not a real potential form.
報い ('reward or punishment', reflecting karmic just-deserts) matches base 報う's own duality ('to reward'/'to retaliate'); kept one-way since 報う itself is a rare classical form.
報い directly mirrors modern 報いる's own reward/retribution duality ('to reward'/'to retaliate'); nothing extra either side.
突き ('thrust, stab, lunge') is the predictable martial/fencing noun form of 'to poke/stab'; kept one-way as a mild safety margin.
Canonical example: 甘み covers 'sweetness' predictably, but base 甘い also commonly means 'naive/lenient', a sense the noun doesn't teach.
味わい's 'charm' sense is a natural but genuinely metaphorical extension (aesthetic charm from 'good taste/flavor') that needs some exposure to fully predict.
思いやり ('consideration, thoughtfulness') is the direct, transparent nominalization of 'to be considerate of' with nothing extra either side.

高み ('height, elevated place') follows the productive adjective+み pattern (quality → a place/degree characterized by it, cf. 深み), reasonably predictable though the idiom 高みの見物 adds a specific connotation.
居眠り ('dozing off while sitting') is the direct, transparent nominalization; kept one-way since the verb 居眠る itself is a rare back-formation rarely encountered standalone.
富み is simply the direct nominal form of 'to be rich/abundant in'; the noun 富 ('wealth') is common knowledge and carries no extra sense.
通し carries the lexicalized culinary sense 'appetizer/amuse-bouche' and the theater term 'full uncut performance', both beyond plain 'letting through'.
流される is the regular passive/spontaneous form ('to drift, be swept away'); base 流す is highly polysemous (broadcast, cancel, shed tears) with senses beyond what this specific passive covers.
寄り's common modern use ('leaning toward', 右寄り) is a predictable metaphorical extension of 'drawing near'; kept one-way given the additional specific sumo wrestling technique sense.
盛り specifically means 'the peak/height of a season' (盛りの桜), a lexicalized temporal sense beyond plain 'to become vigorous'.
怪しげ ('questionable, dubious') is the predictable げ-suffix ('looking/seeming X') form of 怪しい with no unrelated extra sense.
お辞儀 ('a bow') matches base 辞儀 directly; kept one-way since 辞儀 without お is archaic and rarely encountered standalone by learners.
お側 uses the specific literary/courtly reading そば ('to serve at someone's side' 側に仕える) rather than the ordinary がわ reading of 側, a register shift that isn't predictable.
お手洗い directly mirrors base 手洗い's own euphemistic 'restroom/toilet' sense (already listed in the base glosses); the honorific prefix adds nothing new.
恥ずかしがる ('to act bashful/blush') is the fully regular がる-suffix ('show signs of feeling X') pattern from 恥ずかしい, kept one-way as a mild safety margin.
恵み ('blessing, grace') is the direct nominalization of 'to bless/show mercy'; kept one-way given a slight risk of over-narrow religious framing.
現れ ('embodiment, manifestation') is a fairly transparent nominalization ('a manifestation' = 'something that appeared'); kept one-way given the abstraction involved.
詰め is the specific go/shogi term for 'endgame/checkmate' (tsume), a lexicalized domain term beyond plain 'stuffing/packing'.
見習い concretely means 'an apprentice/trainee' (a job-status noun), a specific institutional sense beyond plain 'to imitate/follow an example'.
結ばれる carries the well-known idiomatic romantic sense 'to be united in marriage/love' (二人は結ばれた), not obviously predictable from a plain passive of 'to tie'.
取り返し appears almost exclusively in the fixed idiom 取り返しのつかない ('irreversible'), a specific set-phrase usage rather than a freely predictable noun.
吹っ切れる parallels 吹っ切る closely ('to be dispelled/put behind one' vs 'to get over/forget'), including the shared literal 'burst (of a boil)' sense; nothing hidden either side.
被せる carries the common idiom 'to pin blame on someone' (罪を人に被せる), a lexicalized extension beyond plain 'to cover with something'.
開かれる is the regular passive ('to be held, of a meeting'); base 開く is highly polysemous (a wound opens, a gap widens, a store opens) with senses beyond this specific passive.
強め is the regular め-suffix pattern; base 強い also covers abstract senses (competent, domineering) the purely gradable noun doesn't carry.
締め切り is the fixed, highly conventionalized word for 'deadline'; while metaphorically motivated, it functions as a fixed term rather than a freely predictable noun.
誤魔化し ('cheating, trickery') is the direct, transparent nominalization of 'to deceive/cheat' with no unrelated extra sense.
お先 ('ahead, the future') including the set phrase お先に失礼します stays close to base 先's own 'point, tip, ahead' sense; kept one-way as a safety margin.
色っぽい ('sexy, amorous, erotic') draws on 色's specific romantic/sexual connotation (色気, 色恋), a sense not evident from the plain 'colour/hue' gloss given for the base.
お嬢 carries the cultural stereotype of a pampered young lady (お嬢様 image) alongside a referent shift ('another's daughter'); kept conservative given the added social connotation.
任せ ('leaving everything up to someone else') is the direct, transparent nominalization of 'to entrust/leave to' with no unrelated extra sense.
握り is the very well-known abbreviation for nigiri sushi (握り寿司), a lexicalized culinary sense far beyond plain 'grasping'.
剥がれる is the regular spontaneous/passive counterpart ('to come unstuck, peel off') of 'to tear/peel off', kept one-way as a mild safety margin.
飛び出し ('jumping/running/dashing out') is the direct, transparent nominalization of 'to jump out' with no unrelated extra sense.
責任を持って ('responsibly, properly') functions as a fixed set adverbial phrase whose idiomatic register isn't obviously predictable from the literal 'holding responsibility'.
選ばれる ('to be chosen/elected') is simply the regular passive of 'to choose'; fully predictable with nothing extra either side.
悪さ carries the specific idiom 'mischief' (悪さをする, said of children's naughty behaviour), a countable-event sense not predictable from the abstract quality noun 'badness' alone.
お荷物 ('burden, albatross') matches base 荷物's own 'burden' sense (already in the base glosses); the honorific prefix adds nothing new.
強がる ('to pretend to be tough, bluff') is the fully regular がる-suffix pattern; base 強い also covers broader abstract senses (competent, domineering) the specific 'pretend-strength' idiom doesn't carry.
お決まり means 'the usual/standard thing' (a routine or cliché), a lexicalized sense closely related to お約束's 'trope' sense and beyond plain 'a rule/decision'.
順に is the predictable ni-adverb ('in order, in turn'); base 順 also means 'obedient', a sense the adverb doesn't carry.
ご尤も functions as a fixed conversational response ('you're quite right', sometimes said pointedly/sarcastically), a specific usage pattern beyond the plain adjective 'reasonable'.
包み additionally functions as a counter word ('一包み', a counter for wrapped bundles), a grammatical extra function beyond the plain noun.
明るさ ('brightness') is the predictable noun form; kept one-way given base 明るい's additional figurative 'cheerful (personality)' sense.
引け appears in the fixed idiom 引けを取らない ('to be second to none'), a specific set-phrase sense beyond plain 'closing/leaving'.
戻り ('return, recovery') is the direct, transparent nominalization of 'to return' with no unrelated extra sense.

盛り上がり's dominant modern sense 'climax/excitement' (of a party, mood) is a natural metaphorical extension of 'swelling/rising' that most learners can infer, though it needs some exposure to the collocation.
痛く as an intensifying adverb ('extremely, deeply') is a somewhat literary/classical usage (痛く感激する) not derivable from the modern colloquial 'painful/cringy' sense of 痛い.
